notes: linked_map_ids is left empty: map:j-parc does not exist in this worktree/branch as of 2026-09-18 (a concurrent researcher's task). facility:kamioka-observatory.related_facility_ids already lists facility:j-parc, so once map:j-parc is merged the build's automatic derivation (related_facility_ids with a map, plus beamline:j-parc-neutrino's far_detector_site_ids pointing at this map's own sites) should link the two maps without any authoring change here.

facility:kamioka-observatory's own notes record that the Kamioka Observatory also hosts KAGRA, CANDLES, NEWAGE and XENONnT R&D, and that experiment:kamiokande/experiment:kamland-zen exist as atlas experiment records; none of these have their own site: record in this atlas (only the two mines already in site_ids do), so there is nothing further to draw or list in unlocated[] for them — flagged here as a completeness gap, not a map defect.

Overpass (overpass-api.de and lz4.overpass-api.de) refused every connection attempted this session (curl error 7, 'Failed to connect') for a Mozumi-area building/tunnel-entrance query; unlike the CJPL query earlier in the same session, which succeeded once. summary.plain: The Kamioka Observatory's two underground sites in Gifu, Japan: the Mozumi mine, home to Super-Kamiokande and KamLAND, and the Tochibora mine 8 km south, where Hyper-Kamiokande is being built. Both receive the T2K neutrino beam from J-PARC, 295 km away.
summary.technical: Local map for facility:kamioka-observatory spanning the Mozumi mine (site:kamioka-mozumi-mine-super-kamiokande, site:kamioka-kamland) and the Tochibora mine (site:kamioka-hyper-kamiokande-tochibora), 8 km apart. Super-Kamiokande is drawn as a derived 39.3 m circle around its own surveyed GPS centre; Hyper-Kamiokande as a surveyed point from its 2011 Letter of Intent; KamLAND as the coarse point already on record (no better source was fetched this session). An inferred_direction feature shows the T2K beam's 295 km baseline from J-PARC, cross-checked against the T2K instrumentation paper's own surveyed figure.
